summary.tldr: Repeals the Criminal Code rule that allows parents, teachers and caregivers to use reasonable force to correct a child.
what_it_does: Repeals section 43 of the Criminal Code, which now says schoolteachers, parents and people standing in the place of a parent may use reasonable force by way of correction toward a child or pupil.
Casts off the legal defence that section 43 gives for that kind of force.
Comes into force on the 30th day after royal assent.
summary.background: The bill says it responds to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada’s call to action number 6. Section 43 of the Criminal Code now sets out a defence for reasonable force used by way of correction.
